author: mjn
text: DECISION: Abacus will be a standalone tool (not embedded in beads) with its own SQLite DB, CLI, and MCP server. Beads integration via optional hooks — composable, not coupled. Rationale: different concerns (task tracking vs app modeling), different lifecycles, but same agent ecosystem.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Graph schema is API-first with an Action semantic layer. Auto-scan gives structure (Routes, Entities, Pages). Agents enrich with Actions that bridge Gherkin natural language to technical nodes. Actions are the cumulative knowledge that makes Gherkin-to-implementation possible.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Full BDD cycle — Gherkin → E2E test → implementation. Agent reads Gherkin, queries Abacus for matching Actions, generates step defs + E2E tests (red), then implements backend/frontend code (green). The graph is what makes this feasible without re-exploring the codebase every session.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: New Linear project 'Abacus' in the pcom-mike workspace. This is a distinct initiative serving E2E testing, feature implementation, onboarding, and general codebase understanding. Not scoped to the E2E Testing project alone.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Current state — 382 beads knowledge entries, ALL from contest feature work. Zero entries about e2e, gherkin, playwright, auth flows, or general app structure. This gap is the motivating problem: reactive memories don't capture application shape proactively.

author: mjn
text: FACT: hourly/e2e/ already exists with Playwright + playwright-bdd, 1 feature file (auth/login.feature), 13 step defs, demo + e2e seed scripts. 45+ oRPC contracts, 30+ route files, CompanyOnboarding component exists. The structural data for auto-scan is rich.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Target codebase (hourly) has 45+ oRPC contracts, 100+ Prisma models, 50+ React pages, existing Playwright + playwright-bdd setup with auth/login.feature (13 step defs). Rich dataset for MVP validation.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Match algorithm is tiered (Cucumber expressions → FTS5 fuzzy → LLM-assisted creation) and serves as a GROWTH mechanism. When no Action matches, the algorithm packages graph context as a suggestion for the agent to create a new Action. The graph learns from every feature.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Scanner architecture is pluggable from day 1. Scanner interface with registry, concrete implementations for oRPC, Prisma, React Router. Extensible to Express, GraphQL, etc.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: MCP server uses @modelcontextprotocol/server with stdio transport, Zod v4 for input schemas, better-sqlite3 sync API for instant responses. All logging to stderr.

author: mjn
text: FACT: CLI uses Commander.js + @commander-js/extra-typings for type-safe args. Binary names: abacus, ab. All commands support --json flag.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Switched from TypeScript to Go for core. Reasons: better compiler feedback for agents, single binary distribution, matches beads ecosystem (also Go/cobra), no CGo needed (modernc.org/sqlite). Scanners remain Node.js (BYOASTP).

author: mjn
text: DECISION: BYOASTP (Bring Your Own AST Parser) architecture. Scanners are standalone executables communicating via Scanner Protocol v1 (JSON over stdin/stdout). Abacus core has zero language-specific parsing. Any language can write a scanner.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Go MCP SDK uses mcp.AddTool() with struct-based input schemas (auto-generated via jsonschema tags). StdioTransport for Claude Code. MCP server is a cobra subcommand in the same binary: abacus mcp-server.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Official Go libraries exist for all needed components: MCP SDK (v1.4.0), cucumber-expressions-go, gherkin/go/v38, modernc.org/sqlite. Zero third-party gaps.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: TypeScript compiler messages are poor for agent feedback loops. When Sonnet agents hit TS compiler errors, messages are often cryptic ('Type X is not assignable to Y' with deeply nested generics) and lead to thrashing. Go compiler messages are precise, actionable, and include suggestions ('did you mean X?'). For agent-built tools, compiler feedback quality is a first-class design concern — choose languages where agents can self-correct from error output.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: BYOASTP (Bring Your Own AST Parser) — when a tool needs to parse multiple languages/frameworks, don't embed parsers. Instead, define a versioned JSON protocol over stdin/stdout and spawn parsers as subprocesses. Benefits: (1) core stays language-agnostic, (2) parsers can be written in whatever language parses that stack best, (3) fault isolation — crashing parser can't take down the host, (4) independent versioning, (5) community extensibility without forking. The protocol IS the interface. Trade-off: subprocess startup overhead (~100-500ms), but acceptable for scan-frequency operations.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Match failures as growth signals. When designing a lookup/match system, make the 'not found' path productive. Instead of returning empty, package the search context (what was queried, what related items exist) as a structured creation suggestion. The caller (agent or human) reviews and persists. This transforms every failure into a learning event. Applied in Abacus: Gherkin step with no matching Action → system returns related Routes/Entities/Pages + pre-filled Action template → agent creates Action → future queries succeed. The system gets smarter with each miss.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Go has a complete native ecosystem for building MCP-enabled CLI tools with graph storage: (1) github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk v1.4.0 — official MCP SDK with mcp.AddTool() and StdioTransport, (2) github.com/cucumber/cucumber-expressions-go — pattern matching with parameter extraction, (3) github.com/cucumber/gherkin/go/v38 — Gherkin file parsing, (4) modernc.org/sqlite — pure Go SQLite driver, no CGo needed, (5) github.com/spf13/cobra — CLI framework. Zero third-party gaps. All officially maintained.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: MCP server as cobra subcommand in same binary. Instead of shipping a separate MCP server executable, add 'abacus mcp-server' as a cobra subcommand. Claude Code config points to the same binary: {command: 'abacus', args: ['mcp-server']}. Benefits: single binary distribution, shared code with CLI, no separate install step, version consistency. The subcommand blocks on StdioTransport — all logging must go to stderr since stdout is the JSON-RPC protocol channel.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: When designing inter-process protocols (like Scanner Protocol v1), include: (1) version field for forward compatibility, (2) self-describing scanner metadata (id, name, version), (3) warnings array for partial failures (don't make it all-or-nothing), (4) stats block for observability (filesScanned, durationMs), (5) validation rules that the host checks before ingestion. Publish a JSON Schema file so implementers can validate offline. A good protocol is testable with echo: 'echo {json} | scanner-cmd' should work standalone.

author: mjn
text: FACT: hourly backend is an Express application. oRPC is used for contract definition and client SDK generation, but Express is the actual route infrastructure. Both scanners are essential and complementary: oRPC captures WHAT (typed contracts, schemas), Express captures HOW (middleware, auth guards, route mounting). Don't treat Express as legacy.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Go module cache at /Users/mjn/go/pkg is read-only in the Claude Code sandbox. Must use GOMODCACHE=/tmp/.claude_scratch/gomodcache GONOSUMDB=* GONOSUMCHECK=* for all go commands.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Preserved existing .gitignore entries (.dolt/, *.db) from beads init and appended new Go-specific entries.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: modernc.org/sqlite supports FTS5 and unixepoch() out of the box — no special build tags needed. GOMODCACHE must be an absolute path.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used content-sync FTS5 (content='nodes', content_rowid='rowid') with triggers rather than external-content manual sync, keeping FTS automatically in sync with the nodes table.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Pure-Go SQLite setup with modernc.org/sqlite: driver name is 'sqlite' (NOT 'sqlite3' which is mattn's CGO driver). Pragmas must be individual Exec() calls, not batched. Set WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, cache_size=-64000 (64MB), busy_timeout=5000. If any pragma fails, Close() the db before returning to prevent leaked connections.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: FTS5 content-sync trigger pattern for SQLite. The delete command syntax is counterintuitive: INSERT INTO table_fts(table_fts, rowid, cols) VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.cols). Table name appears as both target and column. UPDATE triggers must delete-then-insert (FTS5 has no native update). content_rowid='rowid' ties to SQLite's implicit rowid — breaks if table uses WITHOUT ROWID.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: SQLite graph adjacency list with enforced types. CHECK constraints on kind columns enforce enums at DB level. UNIQUE(src_id, dst_id, kind) prevents duplicate edges of same kind but allows multiple edge types between same nodes. ON DELETE CASCADE on edges auto-cleans when nodes are deleted. Properties as JSON TEXT DEFAULT '{}' — extensible without migrations, queryable via json_extract(). Adding new kinds requires schema migration (intentional — schema is the contract).

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Cobra CLI with ldflags version injection. Declare 'var Version = "dev"' (must be var, not const — linker can't override constants). Build with '-ldflags "-X full/package/path.Version="'. Full import path required — wrong path silently does nothing. Cobra's rootCmd.Version field + SetVersionTemplate gives --version flag for free. VERSION ?=  with fallback to 'dev'.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used a --dir flag on init command to allow testing in temp directories. This keeps tests isolated without needing to chdir.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: cobra rootCmd is a package-level var, so tests reuse it across test functions. The --dir flag on init avoids test pollution by pointing at t.TempDir().

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Runner splits command string on whitespace (strings.Fields) rather than using shell parsing. This keeps the implementation simple and avoids shell injection. Complex commands can be wrapped in 'bash -c' by the caller.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: echo-scanner.sh test fixture uses heredoc with single-quoted delimiter ('EOF') to avoid variable expansion in the JSON output. The fixture consumes stdin but ignores it — just echoes hardcoded valid ScanOutput.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: ValidateOutput returns []string (error messages) rather than error, making it composable — callers can check len(errs) == 0 and format/join as needed. The runner joins them with semicolons for its error return.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: FTS5 content-sync join requires joining on rowid (n.rowid = fts.rowid), not on id. The content='nodes' and content_rowid='rowid' config in the FTS5 virtual table means FTS stores rowid references, not the text id primary key.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used sql.NullString for nullable fields (source_file, scan_hash) to handle NULL values cleanly in scan operations, converting to *string pointers on the GraphNode struct.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Recursive CTE with UNION (not UNION ALL) for cycle-safe bidirectional graph traversal in SQLite. UNION inherently deduplicates visited nodes, preventing infinite loops in cyclic graphs without maintaining an explicit visited set. Query shape: WITH RECURSIVE connected(id, depth) AS (VALUES(?,0) UNION SELECT e.dst_id, c.depth+1 FROM edges e JOIN connected c ON e.src_id=c.id WHERE c.depth<? UNION SELECT e.src_id, c.depth+1 FROM edges e JOIN connected c ON e.dst_id=c.id WHERE c.depth<?). Two UNION branches traverse both edge directions.

author: mjn
text: FACT: validNodeKinds and validEdgeKinds are duplicated across db/types.go (Go constants) and scanner/validate.go (map[string]bool allowlists). Adding a new node or edge kind requires updating BOTH locations plus the SQLite CHECK constraint in schema.go. These are NOT derived from a single source of truth. This is the primary extensibility gotcha — forgetting one location causes silent validation failures.

author: mjn
text: FACT: RunAll merges scanner outputs by concatenation but does NOT run cross-scanner validation. Edges from scanner A referencing nodes from scanner B pass per-scanner validation but could fail at DB insert time. Also, two scanners emitting the same node ID results in last-write-wins via BulkUpsertNodes. No dedup detection exists at the merge layer. This is acceptable for MVP but needs SyncScanResults logic to handle properly.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Go repository testing with real SQLite via t.TempDir() — no mocking. setupTestDB creates a real in-memory or temp-file SQLite DB with full schema, registered for cleanup via t.Cleanup. This ensures DB behavior (triggers, constraints, FTS5) is tested faithfully. Combined with builder helpers (makeNode, validOutput) that provide default-valid test data where tests modify one field to trigger specific errors.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Subprocess plugin system with fail-open aggregation. RunAll captures per-scanner errors into MergedScanOutput.Errors and continues executing remaining scanners. Callers must check len(merged.Errors) > 0 after RunAll — a nil error return does NOT mean all scanners succeeded. This is the standard pattern for batch operations where partial results are more valuable than all-or-nothing.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: After JSON round-trip through SQLite (MarshalProperties/UnmarshalProperties), Go []string stored in properties becomes []interface{} when read back. Tests must use []any type assertion, not []string.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: ActionService.deleteEdgesFromByKind accesses repo.database directly (unexported field, same package) rather than adding a new method to GraphRepository. This keeps the repository API unchanged per file ownership rules.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: FTS5 BM25 ranks for small test datasets are very small negative numbers (e.g., -0.000003). A threshold of -10.0 incorrectly filters everything out. Default threshold should be 0 to accept all FTS5 results.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used Tokenize() as shared function between FuzzyMatcher and SuggestionBuilder to avoid duplication. Exported it for testability.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used regex-based .feature file parser (stepLineRe matching Given/When/Then/And/But) instead of gherkin-go library. Simpler, more reliable, no API compatibility issues across gherkin versions.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: cobra persistent flags (like --json on rootCmd) persist across Execute() calls in tests since they share the same rootCmd. Tests that depend on flag state must account for this.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: MCP go-sdk v1.4.0 AddTool generic function auto-generates input schema from Go struct tags. Handler signature is func(ctx, *CallToolRequest, InputStruct) (*CallToolResult, any, error). CallToolRequest is ServerRequest[*CallToolParamsRaw]. TextContent needs pointer receiver for Content interface.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used a single queryNodesByKind helper method shared by query_routes, query_entities, query_pages to avoid duplication. Each handler just passes the appropriate NodeKind constant.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Stats handler uses GetNodesByKind with large limit rather than COUNT query since the repo API lacks a count method. This is acceptable for reasonable graph sizes.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: MCP Go SDK v1.4.0 tool registration uses generic AddTool[In, Out](server, tool, handler). Input struct tags: json for field names, jsonschema for descriptions. Handler returns (*CallToolResult, Out, error). Use &TextContent{Text: jsonStr} for response content. Tool names must be [a-zA-Z0-9_.-], max 128 chars. Import as gomcp to avoid package name collision with local mcp/ package.

author: mjn
text: FACT: JSON round-trip through SQLite (MarshalProperties → TEXT → UnmarshalProperties) converts Go []string to []interface{}. Code reading properties back must use type assertion to []any, not []string. This affects gherkin_patterns stored in Action properties.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Regex-based .feature file parser is preferred over gherkin-go library for CLI match/coverage commands. Pattern: stepLineRe matching Given/When/Then/And/But at line start. Simpler, no version compatibility issues, sufficient for step extraction. Full AST parsing only needed if we need Scenario/Feature metadata.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Shared query helper pattern for MCP tools. When multiple tools differ only by a NodeKind filter (query_routes, query_entities, query_pages), use a single private helper method (queryNodesByKind) that accepts the kind as a parameter. Each handler is a thin wrapper. Reduces duplication from N*50 lines to N*5 + 50.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: oRPC scanner uses ts-morph to find .route() PropertyAccessExpression calls, extracts object literal args, then walks the chain upward to find .input()/.output() identifiers. globSync from node:fs handles file discovery. 16 tests (14 unit + 2 integration).

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Prisma scanner uses regex-based parsing (no @prisma/internals dependency). Regex captures model/enum blocks, field attributes, @relation annotations. Only creates edges for owning side (has @relation(fields:...)). 30 tests.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Express scanner detects router.get/post/put/delete direct routes, router.route() chaining, and middleware extraction. Function calls like requireRole('admin') extract just the name. 18 tests.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: React Router scanner parses JSX <Route> elements with ts-morph (needs jsx: react-jsx in tsconfig). Handles nesting via parent walk for path composition, index routes, catch-all, and protection detection via ternary+Navigate pattern. 14 tests.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Scanner Template — all 4 scanners share identical skeleton: (1) index.ts reads ScanInput from stdin, calls parser, writes ScanOutput to stdout; (2) parser.ts has async function returning ScanOutput with try/catch per file → warnings accumulation; (3) types.ts duplicates protocol types (should be shared @abacus/scanner-protocol package); (4) Deterministic IDs: route:{METHOD}-{path}, entity:{ModelName}, page:{fullPath}; (5) Stats tracking: filesScanned, nodesFound, edgesFound, errors, durationMs. Template is identical enough to generate new scanners from.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Regex vs ts-morph for scanners — use regex for non-JS/TS inputs (Prisma schemas, YAML, SQL, .env) and ts-morph for actual TypeScript/JavaScript/JSX source code. The decision boundary is clear: if the input has a TS parser, use it. ts-morph requires skipAddingFilesFromTsConfig:true and noEmit:true to stay fast (parse-only, no type resolution). JSX parsing needs jsx:4 (ReactJSX) in compiler options.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: AST chain walking for fluent APIs — when parsing builder patterns like oc.route({}).input(S).output(S) or router.route('/path').get(h).put(h), the innermost call (.route()) is the deepest AST node. Walk UP via Parent→PropertyAccessExpression→Parent→CallExpression to find chained methods. Use a bounded loop (5-20 iterations) or walk until parent===null. Both oRPC and Express scanners use this technique.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Scanner development checklist — (1) Always emit valid ScanOutput even on fatal errors (Prisma index.ts is the gold standard); (2) Use try/catch per file with warning accumulation, never let one bad file kill the scan; (3) Generate deterministic IDs from content ({kind}:{unique_key}); (4) Set source:'scan' and sourceFile (relative) on all nodes; (5) Return edges:[] and warnings:[] (not undefined) when empty; (6) Only emit edges for relationships your scanner can structurally detect (cross-scanner edges belong in a stitching phase); (7) Test protocol conformance by looping over all nodes asserting required fields.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Scanner code duplication opportunities — (1) resolveGlobs() is copy-pasted between oRPC and Express; (2) ScanOutput types are duplicated 4x across types.ts files; (3) stdin reading has two inconsistent patterns (sync readFileSync vs async chunked); (4) per-file try/catch→warning loop is identical in all ts-morph scanners. These should become a shared @abacus/scanner-protocol package. Prisma scanner is the cleanest reference (separates parsing from output building, most robust error handling, most complete test coverage).

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: React Router JSX scanner nuances — (1) Must handle both JsxSelfClosingElement (<Route .../>) and JsxElement (<Route>children</Route>) with different APIs; (2) Path composition for nested routes requires recursive parent walk (getParentRoutePath); (3) Protected route detection uses heuristic: walk up AST for ConditionalExpression inside JsxExpression where falsy branch contains Navigate; (4) Component extraction unwraps: JsxAttribute→JsxExpression→inner JsxSelfClosingElement→tag name. Most complex of the 4 scanners due to nesting and contextual detection.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: CLI query commands reuse the same GraphRepository/ActionService methods as the MCP server handlers. The CLI is a thin output-formatting layer over the same query API. Shared queryNodesCmd helper handles routes/entities/pages identically.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Shared queryNodesCmd() factory function creates cobra commands for routes/entities/pages. Each specific command file (routes.go, entities.go, pages.go) is ~10 lines calling this factory with NodeKind. Extra columns per kind: routes→METHOD, entities→FIELDS count, pages→PATH.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Cobra persistent BoolVar flags leak between tests in the same package. Once --json is set true by one test, it stays true for subsequent tests using the same rootCmd. Fix: explicitly set --json=false in tests that expect human-readable output.

author: mjn
text: FACT: CLI package now has 33 tests total: 9 init, 8 match/coverage, 16 scan/query. All commands follow the pattern: open DB → create repo/services → query → format output (JSON or table). Shared queryNodesCmd factory generates 3 commands from a single function.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Cobra command factory for kind-filtered queries. When multiple CLI commands differ only by a filter parameter (NodeKind), create a factory function queryNodesCmd(kind, use, short) that returns a pre-configured *cobra.Command. Each concrete command file is ~10 lines calling the factory. Extra columns per kind are handled via a switch inside the factory. Applied: routes.go, entities.go, pages.go all use queryNodesCmd from nodes.go. Reduces N*120 lines to N*10 + 120.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: CLI-as-thin-wrapper-over-services. CLI commands and MCP server handlers call the same underlying services (GraphRepository, ActionService, MatchService, scanner.Runner) — they differ only in output formatting (table vs JSON-RPC). This ensures behavioral parity: if a query works in MCP, it works in CLI. Pattern: open DB → create repo/services → call same method → format for output target.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Cobra persistent BoolVar flags leak between test invocations on the same rootCmd. Once --json is set true by one test's SetArgs+Execute, the bound variable stays true for subsequent tests. Cobra does NOT reset persistent flags to defaults between Execute() calls. Fix: explicitly pass --json=false in tests expecting human-readable output. This affects any persistent flag bound via BoolVar/StringVar.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Scan pipeline — config → runner → node ingest → edge ingest. The scan command: (1) resolves config.yaml path from --db flag path, (2) filters scanners by optional type arg, (3) runs scanner.Runner.RunAll() which spawns subprocesses, (4) converts ScanNode→GraphNode and bulk upserts, (5) ingests edges one-by-one with warn-on-failure (edges may reference cross-scanner nodes not yet ingested). Same pipeline in MCP scanHandler but with different output formatting.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Abacus CLI now has 8 commands beyond init/version: scan, routes, entities, pages, actions (with create subcommand), graph, stats, match, coverage. All support --json flag. 33 CLI tests total across 4 test files. The actions command uses parent+subcommand pattern (actionsCmd.AddCommand(actionsCreateCmd)) for extensibility (future: actions delete, actions update).

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Use mcp.NewInMemoryTransports() from Go MCP SDK for in-process MCP testing. Returns paired (serverTransport, clientTransport) via net.Pipe(). Server_test.go already tests handlers directly — the E2E test layers on transport to prove full JSON-RPC protocol. See .gomodcache/github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk@v1.4.0/mcp/client_example_test.go for client usage.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Existing test helpers: setupTestDB (cli/match_test.go:15-48), setupTestDBWithNodes (cli/query_test.go:17-77), openTestDB/openAndInitTestDB (db/db_test.go:10-28), setupTestServer (mcp/server_test.go:15-42). Echo scanner fixture at testdata/scanners/echo-scanner.sh.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Skills will be delivered as a Claude Code plugin inside the abacus repo. Structure: plugin.json + skills/abacus-validate/SKILL.md + commands/. Anyone who clones abacus and installs the plugin gets the skills. Reference: ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/example-plugin/ for plugin structure.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Claude Code plugin structure: .claude-plugin/plugin.json (name, description, author) + commands/ dir with markdown files. Commands use YAML frontmatter (description, argument-hint). Body is imperative instructions to the executing agent. Agents dir for autonomous agents with model/color frontmatter.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Created 6 slash commands (abacus-scan, abacus-query, abacus-graph, abacus-coverage, abacus-new-scanner, abacus-validate) as commands/ markdown files. All use --json for programmatic output. abacus-validate doubles as aba-zca.20 implementation.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Scanner config format in config.yaml uses map[string]ScannerConfig where keys are scanner IDs, not array entries. Skills reference the CLI commands directly via Bash tool.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: detectProject monorepo support — must scan subdirectory package.json files (backend/, frontend/) and Prisma paths (backend/prisma/schema.prisma). Root package.json in monorepos often only has client deps. oRPC detection broadened to any @orpc/* prefix.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: abacus init --force + scanner auto-detection required 3 iterations to work against real project (hourly). Issues: (1) old binary on PATH, (2) no --force flag to re-detect, (3) monorepo structure with deps split across subdirectory package.json files and Prisma in backend/prisma/. Each was only discoverable by testing against a real project, not unit tests.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Scanners must have sensible defaults when options are empty/undefined. Express defaults routeGlobs to ['**/*.ts','**/*.js'], oRPC defaults contractGlobs to ['**/*.ts'], React Router auto-detects route files from common locations (src/routes.tsx etc), Prisma falls back through backend/prisma/schema.prisma, server/prisma/schema.prisma, etc. Without defaults, scanners crash with 'globs is not iterable' when config has no options.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Scanner robustness pattern — always use optional chaining + nullish coalescing for options: const globs = options?.routeGlobs ?? ['**/*.ts']. Never trust that config.yaml options will be populated. Defense in depth: init populates defaults AND scanners handle missing options.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Three scanners generated duplicate node/edge IDs because ID templates lacked sufficient discriminating context. Express/oRPC used route:${METHOD}-${path} which collided when multiple router files defined same relative paths (GET /, POST /, GET /:id). Prisma used edge:entity:${model}-field_relation-entity:${target} which collided when a model had multiple FKs to the same target entity. Root cause: ID generation assumed 1:1 mapping between ID components and real entities, but real-world projects have many-files-to-same-paths and many-fields-to-same-target patterns.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Scanner ID uniqueness rule — every node/edge ID must encode ALL dimensions necessary for global uniqueness: (1) entity kind, (2) source file path (normalized), (3) local discriminator. Mental test: if someone copy-pasted the source file to a second location, would IDs collide? If yes, missing a dimension. Express/oRPC fix: route:${METHOD}-${routerName}:${path} where routerName derived from relPath via deriveRouterName(). Prisma fix: edge:entity:${model}-field_relation:${fieldName}-entity:${target}.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: deriveRouterName/deriveContractName helper pattern — strips common prefixes (src/, backend/, routes/, routers/, api/), file extensions (.routes.ts, .router.ts, .ts, .js), and trailing /index from relPath to produce a stable human-readable namespace. E.g. backend/routes/users.routes.ts → users, src/contracts/auth/login.ts → auth/login. Fallback returns original relPath if stripping produces empty string.

author: mjn
text: FACT: RunAll merges scanner outputs by concatenation with NO cross-scanner dedup detection. Two scanners emitting the same node ID results in last-write-wins via BulkUpsertNodes. This means ID uniqueness must be enforced at the scanner level, not the merge layer. Future improvement: add a runtime Set<string> collision detector in the ingestion pipeline as a safety net.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Chose to derive router/contract names from file paths rather than from code-level identifiers (variable names like 'usersRouter'). Rationale: file paths are always available and stable, while variable names require additional AST analysis, may be inconsistent, and don't work for default exports. The deriveXxxName() approach is O(1) string manipulation vs O(n) AST traversal.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Made ignorePaths project-level (project.ignorePaths in config.yaml) rather than per-scanner. Rationale: most ignores (node_modules, dist, tests) apply to all scanners. Per-scanner already has inclusion globs (routeGlobs, contractGlobs). Project-level avoids redundant config. Passed via ScanInput JSON so scanners receive it automatically.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: ignorePaths matching uses prefix comparison on relative paths: m === ip || m.startsWith(ip + '/'). This matches both exact directory names (dist) and path prefixes (src/demo). All 4 TS scanners use identical predicate. Go side passes the array through ScanInput.IgnorePaths. Default ignores set during abacus init: node_modules, dist, build, .git.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: SQLite UNIQUE(src_id, dst_id, kind) on edges table was too restrictive for field_relation edges. When a Prisma model has multiple FK fields to the same target (e.g. Company.logoFile and Company.iconFile both → FileUpload), same-kind edges between the same node pair are valid. Fix: dropped the UNIQUE constraint, kept id PRIMARY KEY for row-level uniqueness. Schema version bumped from 1→2 with auto-migration (drop+recreate) on version mismatch since scan data is ephemeral.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Express scanner within-file duplicate route IDs occur when test specs or demo files define multiple routes with the same method+path. Fix: added Set<string> tracking in extractRouteNodes — when a duplicate ID is detected, append #2, #3 etc. Also added hardcoded test file exclusion filter: /(\.spec\.|\.test\.|__tests__|\/tests?\/)/.test(f). The ignorePaths config provides the user-configurable layer on top.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: ignorePaths implementation spans Go config layer and all 4 TS scanners. Go side: ProjectConfig.IgnorePaths → ScanInput.IgnorePaths JSON field → each scanner receives it. TS side: each scanner's resolveGlobs/file-finding filters matched files using prefix comparison: m === ip || m.startsWith(ip + '/'). Default ignores set during abacus init: node_modules, dist, build, .git. Users add project-specific ignores (src/demo, tests) to config.yaml.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Live progress in CLI scan commands — instead of using RunAll() which batches everything, iterate scanners individually with RunScanner() and print progress to stderr between calls. Format: 'Scanning with <id>... done (N nodes, N edges, Nms)'. Progress goes to os.Stderr so --json stdout is unaffected. Gate with showProgress = \!quiet && \!jsonFlag.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Five-layer duplicate prevention for graph scanners — (1) File-path prefix in node IDs for cross-file uniqueness (route:GET-users:/), (2) Field name in edge IDs for multi-FK disambiguation (field_relation:fieldName), (3) DB constraint relaxation (drop UNIQUE(src,dst,kind), keep id PK), (4) Within-file Set+counter dedup for same-path routes in one file (#2 suffix), (5) ignorePaths config for directory-level exclusion. Each layer catches a different class of duplicate. No single fix is sufficient for real-world projects.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Edge ingestion used INSERT (not upsert), causing UNIQUE constraint warnings on re-scan. Fix: changed to INSERT OR REPLACE in repository.go InsertEdge(). Now edges upsert like nodes do via BulkUpsertNodes. Re-scanning the same project produces zero warnings. This was masked initially because first scans had no prior data.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: React Router scanner page IDs (page:${path}) duplicate across files when App.tsx and MainApp.tsx both define the same routes (e.g. / and /organization). Fix: same Set+counter dedup pattern as Express scanner — seenIds Set tracks across all files, appends #2 suffix on collision.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: React Router scanner auto-detection was too narrow — only checked 6 hardcoded paths (src/routes.tsx etc). Real projects use App.tsx, MainApp.tsx. Fix: (1) expanded hardcoded list to include App.tsx, MainApp.tsx, frontend/ variants, (2) added glob fallback that searches all *.tsx/*.jsx files for '<Route', 'createBrowserRouter', 'createRoutesFromElements' content.

author: mjn
text: FACT: CLI query commands (routes, entities, pages) had a hardcoded default limit of 50, causing truncated output that looked like incomplete data. Changed default to 1000 and flag help to '0 = all'. The limit flag is defined in queryNodesCmd factory in nodes.go.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: FTS5 tokenizer must strip ALL non-alphanumeric chars, not just common punctuation. Characters like / * + - ^ ~ are FTS5 query syntax and cause 'syntax error near' if they reach the MATCH clause. The fix: iterate bytes and keep only a-z 0-9, instead of Trim with a limited charset.

author: mjn

author: mjn

author: mjn

author: mjn

author: mjn

author: mjn

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Scanner protocol phase extension — add Phase to config, split runner into explicit phase-filtered passes, use lightweight ScanNodeRef for cross-process data, add source_scanner to edges for provenance. Generalizes to any future phase (enrich, validate).

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: File-level entity-reference cache (Map<filePath, Set<entityName>>) is the #1 perf lever — ts-morph caches ASTs natively but analysis results must be cached manually. Without it: O(routes × barrel_fanout). With it: O(1) per repeated visit.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Schema version bumps from 2→3 trigger full table drop+recreate via InitSchema. This is safe during dev but will need a migration strategy before production use.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: ValidateOutput takes knownNodeIDs map[string]bool (nil = scan-phase behavior). Runner passes nil. The link-phase runner (bead aba-iu1.2) will populate this from ExistingNodes.

author: mjn
text: FACT: ScanNodeRef has 4 fields: ID, Kind, Name, SourceFile. No Properties, no Label. Intentionally minimal to reduce stdin payload and avoid leaking scanner metadata.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Edge provenance uses nullable source_scanner TEXT column with index. InsertEdge passes it through as *string. Null means legacy/unknown scanner origin.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: BulkUpsertEdges uses FK-tolerant transaction pattern — checks strings.Contains(err, 'FOREIGN KEY constraint failed') per-row and continues. This gives best-effort semantics for cross-scanner edges where referenced nodes may not exist yet.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: RunScanner signature changed to accept knownNodeIDs map[string]bool as 4th param. Scan-phase callers pass nil. Link-phase callers pass map built from ExistingNodes. This lets ValidateOutput accept cross-scanner edge references.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Two-pass CLI scan flow — DB opens between phases. Scan-phase runs first (60s timeout), nodes ingested, then link-phase (5min timeout) receives ExistingNodes. When user filters to a link-phase scanner, existing nodes come from DB query instead of scan-phase results. Stale edges deleted by source_scanner before BulkUpsertEdges.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Two-pass scanner execution requires DB to open between phases. Scan-phase runs all phase=scan scanners (60s timeout), ingests nodes+edges, then link-phase runs phase=link scanners (5min timeout) with ExistingNodes populated. When user filters to a standalone link-phase scanner (e.g. 'abacus scan linker'), existing nodes must come from DB query (GetNodeRefsByKinds) since there are no scan-phase results in that run.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: FK-tolerant bulk transactions in Go/SQLite — when bulk-inserting edges that may reference nodes from other scanners, check each stmt.Exec error for 'FOREIGN KEY constraint failed', log a warning, and continue. Commit the transaction with all successful rows. This gives best-effort semantics where partial results are more valuable than all-or-nothing. Pattern: tx.Begin → stmt.Prepare → loop(Exec, check FK, continue) → tx.Commit.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Caller-controlled phase orchestration — the Runner stays a dumb subprocess executor (RunScanner runs one command). The CLI scan.go owns orchestration: separating scanners by phase, controlling execution order, managing data flow between phases (ScanNodeRef collection), and handling different timeout/ingestion strategies per phase. This is better than baking phase awareness into Runner because: (1) Runner stays simple and testable, (2) MCP server can implement its own phase orchestration later, (3) separation of concerns.

author: mjn
text: FACT: MCP server (mcp/server.go) uses RunAll which only runs scan-phase scanners. It does NOT support link-phase execution yet. When adding link-phase support to MCP, the scanHandler needs the same two-pass logic as CLI scan.go: filter by phase, ingest scan nodes first, then run linkers with ExistingNodes. This is a future task, not in scope for aba-iu1.2.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Stale edge cleanup is scoped by source_scanner column. DELETE FROM edges WHERE source_scanner = ? runs BEFORE BulkUpsertEdges for each linker. This prevents phantom relationships from accumulating across re-scans while preserving: (1) scan-phase edges (source_scanner is NULL), (2) manually-created edges (source_scanner is NULL), (3) edges from other linker scanners. Each linker only cleans up its own edges.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: When adding a parameter to a widely-called function (RunScanner gained knownNodeIDs), use a nilable type (map[string]bool) so existing callers can pass nil for backward-compatible behavior. All 9 call sites updated: 7 pass nil (scan-phase), 2 pass populated map (link-phase). The ValidateOutput function already accepted this param — the change just threaded it through RunScanner.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Phase config has no validation — a typo like phase: 'lnik' silently defaults to scan phase. Need to add phase validation in config.Load() or the scan loop. Valid values: 'scan', 'link', or empty (defaults to scan). This is a low-effort fix that prevents silent misconfiguration.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Link-phase scanner output nodes are silently dropped — scan.go only processes out.Edges from linkers, ignoring out.Nodes. If a link-phase scanner emits nodes, they vanish with no warning. Should either reject explicitly or document this contract.

author: mjn
text: FACT: BulkUpsertEdges FK violations are logged via log.Printf but NOT returned to the CLI caller — so they don't appear in scanResult.Warnings. The user sees edge count but can't tell which edges were skipped. Future improvement: return violations as structured data alongside the count.

author: mjn

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: ts-morph's in-memory file system (useInMemoryFileSystem: true with createSourceFile) is perfect for testing import chain tracing — you can create complete multi-file import graphs without touching disk. 20 tests run in <1s.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Separated matcher.ts (Prisma detection) from tracer.ts (import walking). Tracer delegates to matcher for entity discovery at each file. This keeps concerns clean and allows matcher to be independently testable.

author: mjn
text: FACT: findPrismaAccesses returns entity node IDs (e.g., entity:User), not entity names. The tracer's file-level cache stores IDs directly. Initial agent implementation had a cache consistency bug where cache stored names but lookup expected IDs.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: When ts-morph Project has no tsconfig, use numeric enum values for ModuleKind (99=ESNext), ModuleResolutionKind (100=Node16), ScriptTarget (99=ESNext) to avoid importing compiler-internal enum types.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: TS linker scanner architecture — 4 modules in pipeline: index.ts (stdin/stdout IO, builds routeNodes/entityByName maps from ExistingNodes) → parser.ts (ts-morph Project setup, route iteration, edge dedup via Set) → tracer.ts (depth-limited DFS through imports, visited-set cycle protection, file-level entity cache) → matcher.ts (PrismaClient variable resolution via 3 heuristics, PropertyAccessExpression chain walking for prisma.model.method() detection). Linker emits only edges (nodes: never[]), edge kind: touches_entity, edge ID: edge:${routeId}-touches_entity-${entityId}, tracePath in properties for debugging.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: oRPC handler resolution is fundamentally harder than Express. Express routes have handler metadata co-located in the route's source file. oRPC contracts and implementations live in different files — the linker must reverse-search for files that import the contract and call .handler()/.func(). Current unit tests only cover direct Prisma access and import chains. Integration test (aba-iu1.6) must validate oRPC routes specifically.

author: mjn
text: FACT: touches_entity edge format — ID: edge:${routeNodeId}-touches_entity-${entityNodeId}, srcId: routeNodeId, dstId: entityNodeId, kind: touches_entity, properties: { tracePath: string[] }. Deduplication required: same route→entity pair via multiple import paths should emit one edge. tracePath records first-discovered path (DFS order, not necessarily shortest).

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: When delegating code to Sonnet agents, explicitly specify the data type at every interface boundary. Don't say 'cache the entities' — say 'cache the entity node IDs (e.g., entity:User), not the entity names (e.g., user)'. The cache consistency bug (names vs IDs) was caught in review but would have been prevented by more precise prompts.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: File-level entity cache must be shared ACROSS route traces, not scoped inside a single traceImports call. Within one call, the visited set prevents any file from being visited twice, making the cache unreachable. The cache only provides value when Route A and Route B share import chains (e.g., both import userService.ts) — the cache skips re-analyzing the shared file on the second route's trace. Fix: accept fileEntityCache as a parameter, create once in processRoutes, pass to each traceImports call.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Critical cache bug in tracer.ts — fileEntityCache stores only direct findPrismaAccesses results, not transitive entities from imports. When cache hit occurs (line 54-61), it returns early without tracing imports. First route gets full DFS, subsequent routes get only direct-entity cache hits (usually 0 for service files). Fix: traceFile must return full transitive entity set and cache that.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Depth-poisoned cache — fileEntityCache is depth-unaware. A file visited at depth 7 (remaining=1) caches a tiny entity set. When later visited at depth 0 (remaining=8), the cache returns the tiny set. Fix: cache entries must store the remaining depth at which they were explored. Only use cache when currentRemaining <= cachedRemaining.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Two cache bugs found and fixed in tracer.ts: (1) Cache stored only direct entities, not transitive — fixed by making traceFile return Set<string> and caching full transitive set. (2) Cache was depth-unaware — a file visited at depth 7 cached a shallow result that poisoned later visits at depth 0. Fixed by storing remainingDepth with each cache entry and only serving cache hits when currentRemaining <= cachedRemaining.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Two interacting cache bugs caused the linker to link only 1/180 routes (358 edges instead of 19,253). Bug 1: fileEntityCache stored only direct findPrismaAccesses results, not transitive entities from imports — traceFile was void so child entities never propagated upward for caching. Bug 2: cache was depth-unaware — a file visited at depth 7 (remaining=1) cached a tiny entity set that poisoned later visits at depth 0 (remaining=8). The bugs compounded: fix 1 alone gave 10/180 routes because depth-poisoning still limited most routes. Both fixes together gave 180/180 routes linked.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Depth-aware transitive DFS cache — when caching results of a depth-limited recursive traversal shared across multiple entry points: (1) the recursive function must RETURN its full transitive result set (direct + child results), not void; (2) cache entries must store {entities, remainingDepth} not just entities; (3) cache hits only valid when currentRemaining <= cachedRemaining; (4) overwrites are safe because deeper exploration is always a superset. Without (1), cache stores partial results. Without (2-3), shallow-first visits poison deeper-later visits.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: DFS cache bug detection — symptoms: (a) order-dependent results (reordering entry points changes output), (b) first-one-works-rest-fail (first traversal correct, subsequent get cached wrong results), (c) shallow results for deep chains. Invariants to assert: transitivity (cached set for N superset of union of children's cached sets), monotonicity (higher depth budget => superset of lower budget result), idempotency (clearing cache doesn't change result). Test strategy: diamond dependency graph with two entry points sharing an intermediate file.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: [SUPERSEDES earlier file-level cache pattern] Corrected tracer cache design: Map<filePath, {entities: Set<string>, remainingDepth: number}>. traceFile returns Set<string> (transitive closure). Cache hit guard: remainingDepth <= cached.remainingDepth. The visited set is per-trace (per route) for cycle protection; the cache is shared across routes for performance. Cache overwrites happen naturally when a file is re-explored with higher depth budget.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Hourly project integration test baseline (2026-03-07): 1001 nodes (750 routes, 179 entities, 72 pages), 19253 edges (247 field_relation from Prisma, 19006 touches_entity from linker-ts). All 180 Express src routes linked (avg ~106 entities each due to barrel file fan-out). 390 oRPC routes unlinked (contract sourceFile, needs reverse-import resolution — aba-l55). Pipeline: 13.8s total, 0 errors, 5 scanners.

author: mjn
text: FACT: DFS cache safety rules — a shared DFS cache is SAFE when: results are deterministic, function runs to completion (no depth limit), and result depends only on the subgraph (not arrival path). DANGEROUS when: depth-bounded search (same node at different remaining depths yields different results), caching partial/local results without transitive closure, or multiple independent traversals sharing a cache with different budgets. Core invariant: a cache entry is valid iff the cached value is correct for EVERY future caller that could look it up.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Chose depth-only approach (not barrel detection) as the first step. Depth property on edges lets consumers filter by hop distance. Barrel detection can layer on top later without refactoring — just adds via_barrel/barrel_file to same properties column.

author: mjn
text: FACT: depth semantics — 0 = entity in the route handler file itself, 1 = one import hop away, N = N hops. Stored in edge properties.depth alongside existing tracePath. TraceResult.entities changed from Map<string, string[]> to Map<string, { tracePath: string[], depth: number }>.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: depth is always equal to tracePath.length - 1 (both derived from same DFS depth parameter). Kept as explicit field for SQL query ergonomics (json_extract without array length computation). First-discovered-wins semantics means DFS visit order determines depth, not shortest path.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Layered edge metadata for graph noise reduction — when a DFS-based linker produces too many edges (e.g., barrel files causing 111 entity connections per route), add metadata to edges rather than removing them. Layer 1: depth (import hop count) on every edge, enabling WHERE depth <= 3 filters. Layer 2 (future): via_barrel boolean flag for barrel-traversed edges. Layer 3 (future): configurable skip patterns. Each layer is purely additive — stored in the edge's JSON properties column, no schema migration needed. Consumers choose their own noise threshold.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Barrel file noise root cause — repositories/index.ts re-exports 80+ individual repository files. authz.middleware.ts imports location.service → repositories/index.ts. Since most routes import authz.middleware, every route transitively reaches every repository, producing ~111 entity connections per route (19,006 total edges across 180 routes). The connections are technically correct but make every route look equally connected. Solution: annotate edges with import depth so consumers can distinguish direct (depth 1-2) from transitive barrel-induced (depth 5+) connections. Implementation required changing only TraceResult.entities value type from string[] to {tracePath, depth} and emitting depth in edge properties — 3 files, ~20 lines of production code changed.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Four approaches considered for barrel file noise: (1) stop at barrel files — aggressive, may miss real relationships, (2) weighted/depth edges — preserves all data, consumers filter, (3) barrel detection + depth hybrid — best accuracy but more complex, (4) configurable skip patterns — user-controlled but fragile. Chose depth-only (#2) because: zero data loss, backward compatible (new JSON key in existing properties column), trivial to implement (depth already tracked in DFS stack), and hybrid (#3) layers cleanly on top later without refactoring. The key insight: annotate rather than filter — let consumers decide their noise threshold.

author: mjn
text: FACT: DFS first-discovered-wins semantics — the entities Map uses if(\!entities.has(id)) guard, meaning the first DFS path to discover an entity sets its depth permanently. In DFS, this is import-order-first, NOT shortest-path-first. If handler imports serviceA (entity at depth 3) before serviceB (same entity at depth 1), depth 3 is recorded. For most real codebases this is fine because direct imports are listed before transitive middleware, but it's not guaranteed. Cache hits compound this: when fileEntityCache returns cached entities at a cache-hit file's depth, tracePath is truncated at the cache boundary (shows path to cached file, not the leaf where prisma.model.method() lives). Both are acceptable approximations for the noise-reduction use case.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used two-pass approach for reverse resolution — first pass traces normally, second pass lazily loads all tsconfig files and searches for handler files that import the contract. This avoids loading the full project graph when not needed (Express routes work without it).

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: ts-morph moduleResolution must be set to Bundler (100) for reliable import resolution of .ts files. Node16/NodeNext resolution requires .js extensions on relative imports, which prevents ts-morph from resolving .ts source files in the project. The findHandlerFiles function also includes a path-based fallback for cases where ts-morph can't resolve imports natively.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Handler detection uses text search for .handler( and .func( patterns combined with import resolution. This is simpler than AST-walking for the oRPC handler pattern and works reliably. The two-stage filter (imports contract + has handler call) is specific enough to avoid false positives.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Integration results — hourly now has 60,767 linker edges (was 19,006). 381/390 oRPC routes linked via reverse-import (41,761 edges). Express routes unchanged at 180/360. 9 oRPC routes unlinked (missing handler files). Warnings 570→180. Performance 14.9s (was 13.8s, 1s overhead for tsconfig loading).

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: The config YAML option name is 'tsconfig' but the TypeScript code expected 'tsConfigPath'. This mismatch meant the linker was falling back to projectRoot/tsconfig.json instead of backend/tsconfig.json. The fix was to accept both option names.
