author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Cross-package import resolution doesn't work with ts-morph because npm packages export from dist/, not src/. Handler files import '@hourly/api-client' which resolves to dist/index.js, not the source contract file. Name-based matching (contract break.ts → handler break.handlers.ts) is the reliable fallback for monorepo cross-package contract/handler patterns.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: The tracer's visited set was returning empty sets for already-visited files, poisoning the fileEntityCache when shared dependencies (like repositories/index.ts) were reached through multiple import paths in the same trace. Fix: when a file is already visited, return cached entities from fileEntityCache instead of empty set. The visited set still prevents infinite recursion for circular imports (where no cache entry exists yet).

author: mjn
text: FACT: The checklist.handlers.ts trace chain (checklist.service → alertInstance.service → location.service → repositories/index) was poisoning location.service.ts cache with 0 entities because repositories/index.ts was already in the visited set from an earlier path through checklist.service → repositories/index. Similarly, compensation handler poisoned incentive.service.ts. This affected exactly 2 of 46 contracts — the ones whose services happened to be reachable through other handlers' import chains.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: tracer.ts visited-set cache poisoning bug. When tracing import chains, the visited set (per-trace) prevents re-visiting files to avoid infinite recursion. But it was returning empty Set() for ALL already-visited files, even when those files had been fully explored and their entities cached in fileEntityCache. This caused cache poisoning: when shared dependencies (e.g., repositories/index.ts) were reached through multiple import paths in the same trace, only the FIRST path got the real entities. The second path got empty, which then cached intermediate files (e.g., location.service.ts) with 0 entities. All subsequent traces hitting those cached files inherited the wrong 0-entity result. Concrete example: checklist.handlers.ts trace visited repositories/index.ts at depth 2, then later reached location.service.ts at depth 3 which also imports repositories/index.ts — but at depth 4 the visited check returned empty, so location.service.ts was cached with 0 entities. This poisoned location.handlers.ts trace in the second pass.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: When implementing DFS with both a visited-set (cycle prevention) and a results-cache (memoization), the visited-set check must NOT blindly return empty. Correct pattern: (1) if depth > maxDepth → empty, (2) if visited AND cached → return cached.entities (already fully explored), (3) if visited AND NOT cached → empty (circular import, still being explored), (4) not visited → proceed with normal trace. The key insight: visited+cached means 'already computed, safe to reuse'; visited+not-cached means 'currently computing, would cause infinite loop'.

author: mjn
text: FACT: In the hourly project, the bug manifested for exactly 2 of 46 oRPC contracts (location, incentive) because their service files happened to be reachable through OTHER handlers' import chains. checklist.service.ts imports alertInstance.service.ts which imports location.service.ts. compensation handler reaches incentive.service.ts. These cross-domain service imports caused the shared repositories/index.ts to be visited first through the 'wrong' path, poisoning the cache. The bug is NOT specific to these 2 contracts — any service file reachable through multiple import paths in the same trace would be affected.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Fixed by checking fileEntityCache when visited.has(filePath) returns true, instead of blindly returning empty Set(). The fix is minimal (10 lines) and preserves circular-import safety: files currently being explored (visited but NOT cached) still return empty. Only files that completed their full DFS traversal and were cached return their cached entities. This avoids the need for more complex solutions like tracking 'in-progress' vs 'completed' states separately, or restructuring the entire cache architecture.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Debugging cache-related bugs in graph traversals: (1) reproduce reliably with a test that uses the exact same data size as production, (2) track WHEN cache entries are first created and BY WHICH caller, (3) compare cache state between working (isolation) and failing (full dataset) scenarios. The key debugging technique was adding 'first cached by' tracking that logged which handler trace set each cache entry — this immediately revealed that location.service.ts was being cached by the checklist handler (wrong context) before the location handler could trace it.

author: mjn
text: FACT: This is the THIRD cache bug in tracer.ts. Bug 1: traceFile was void, so child entities never propagated for caching. Bug 2: cache was depth-unaware — shallow visits poisoned deep visits. Bug 3 (this one): visited-set returned empty for already-visited files, ignoring cached results. All three follow the same meta-pattern: DFS cache invalidation assumptions that break when multiple traversal paths converge on shared nodes. The regression test 'shared dependency visited through multiple paths returns entities for all paths' specifically guards against Bug 3.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: INSERT OR REPLACE in SQLite performs DELETE+INSERT, resetting DEFAULT(unixepoch()) columns. ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE preserves them. Same principle as UpsertNode — always prefer ON CONFLICT for upsert semantics.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Removed 3 duplicate depth tracking tests (depth 0/1/2) that were exact duplicates of existing tracer tests (direct/2-hop/3-hop). Kept multi-entity depth test as the only unique one. Unwrapped from describe('depth tracking') to top-level tracer test.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Exported DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH from tracer.ts (where it's used for the core DFS) and imported it in parser.ts. Tracer is the canonical owner since it implements the depth-limited traversal.

author: mjn
text: FACT: DFS first-discovered-wins depth is determined by import declaration order in source files, not graph topology. The guard is entities.has(entityId) at 3 locations in tracer.ts — once set, an entity's tracePath+depth is immutable for that trace.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Applied plan review feedback. 10 recommendations applied across 2 beads. Key changes: (1) added linker-ts as 5th scanner with two-phase execution, (2) cut from 9 to 5 test scenarios — merged query tests into pipeline subtests, dropped idempotency and error handling, (3) right-sized fixture to minimum cross-scanner composition, (4) added TestMain for scanner build verification, (5) increased timeout to 120s, (6) deferred helpers_test.go.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Fixture has 5 files total: package.json, backend/routes/users.ts (Express+Prisma+contract import), backend/prisma/schema.prisma (User+Post), contracts/users.ts (3 oRPC routes), src/App.tsx (3 React Router pages). No node_modules, no tsconfig — scanners use AST-only analysis.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Kept the Express route file as the single cross-scanner integration point — it imports PrismaClient (for touches_entity edges) AND the oRPC contract (for cross-file import tracing). This maximizes linker-ts coverage with one file.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Cross-scanner integration fixture design — one 'hub' file (backend/routes/users.ts) imports from multiple scanner domains (PrismaClient from @prisma/client, contract from contracts/users.ts) while itself being an Express route. This hub pattern creates cross-scanner edges: Express route → touches_entity → Prisma entity, with linker-ts tracing imports transitively through the contract file. Minimum viable fixture: one hub file + one file per scanner domain + package.json listing deps.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Abacus scanner test fixtures need NO node_modules, NO tsconfig.json, and NO installed dependencies. All 5 scanners (Express, Prisma, React Router, oRPC, linker-ts) work purely via AST analysis with ts-morph or regex. package.json only needs dep names listed for abacus init auto-detection. This means synthetic fixtures can be tiny (5 files, ~100 lines total) and checked into git with zero setup.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Express and oRPC scanners produce colliding route node IDs when scanning the same project (both derive routerName 'users' from backend/routes/users.ts and contracts/users.ts respectively). Route ID format route:METHOD-routerName:path causes 2 collisions out of 6 routes, yielding 4 unique routes after BulkUpsertNodes. Last-processed scanner wins (oRPC overwrites Express).

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: MCP Go SDK uses ServerSessionOptions (not SessionOptions) for Server.Connect(). Added Connect(ctx, transport) and Close() methods to AbacusServer to enable in-process testing via NewInMemoryTransports() without exposing the inner gomcp.Server.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Each test function runs the full scan pipeline independently (5 scanner subprocesses per test × 5 tests = 25 runs). The tiny fixture (5 files) keeps total runtime at ~5s. This is simpler than caching scanner output across tests and ensures complete isolation.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: AbacusServer needs sync.Once for db.Close() because Run() defers Close and tests call Close explicitly. Without it, double-close is possible. Fixed during review.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: maxAllowedDepth=10 as package-level const in mcp/server.go. Clamp applied in handler (not in GetConnected) so internal callers retain full control. 10 is generous — most useful traversals are 2-3 hops.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: CountNodesByKind uses SELECT COUNT(*) as a single QueryRow call. Stays on GraphRepository (not a separate stats service) since it's just a query variant alongside GetNodesByKind.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Placed ToGraphNodes in scanner/protocol.go (not a new convert.go) since it's a natural companion to the ScanNode type defined there. Added db import to scanner package — no circular dependency risk since db is a leaf package with no imports from scanner.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Review of .21.3/.4/.5 found 0 P1 issues in the changes themselves. Most findings (5/7) were pre-existing issues noticed in surrounding code. The three changes are architecturally sound: scanner→db dependency forms valid DAG, max_depth cap in handler is correct layer, COUNT(*) is properly indexed.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Limit capping follows same pattern as max_depth cap — const maxAllowedLimit=500 clamped in handler, not in repository. Keeps internal callers unrestricted.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Two functions (ToGraphEdges, ToGraphEdgesWithSource) rather than one with optional param. Matches Go idiom of explicit function names over bool/pointer flags. Same pattern as ToGraphNodes — converter lives in scanner/protocol.go alongside the types it converts.

author: mjn
text: FACT: CountAllNodesByKind uses GROUP BY so kinds with 0 nodes are absent from the map. statsHandler fills in zeros by iterating the known kinds list. Map lookup on missing key returns zero-value int (0) in Go, so this works naturally.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Replaced double-CTE with CTE-once + IN-clause strategy. CTE runs once for nodes, edges fetched with WHERE src_id IN (...) AND dst_id IN (...). Args array is 2×len(nodes) — same IDs for both IN clauses. Dead nodeSet map removed.

author: mjn
text: FACT: maxGetConnectedDepth=50 as package-level const in repository.go. Generous ceiling — handler caps at 10, CLI at whatever user passes. Defense-in-depth: if a new caller forgets to clamp, GetConnected won't explode.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used kind (db.NodeKind) instead of use (command name) in queryNodesCmd Long text so it reads 'List all route nodes' not 'List all routes nodes'

author: mjn
text: FACT: cobra/doc GenManTree and GenMarkdownTree generate from the command tree at runtime. DisableDefaultCmd on CompletionOptions hides the auto-generated completion command from docs. go get github.com/spf13/cobra/doc upgraded cobra from v1.9.1 to v1.10.2

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Graph serves as INDEX into source code, not a pattern store. Agent reads actual source files to learn patterns. Graph tells it WHICH files to look at.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Use generic 'module' node kind with role in properties (service, repository, helper, etc.) rather than separate NodeService/NodeRepository kinds. Single 'delegates_to' edge kind for the chain. Minimizes schema changes while staying extensible.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Classification of intermediate files (service vs repository vs helper) is configurable per-project in .abacus/config.yaml. Default config uses convention-based heuristics: *service* → service, *repository*/*repo* → repository. abacus-validate will help users configure this interactively.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: For now, agent MIRRORS existing patterns exactly (consistency over improvement). Future: beads provides compounding knowledge layer for continuous improvement suggestions.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Coverage checker works through ACTION nodes (step → action → {route, entity, page}), NOT by traversing route→entity edges. The genesis path verification needs actions to also reference intermediate module nodes, or the agent needs to traverse from route through delegates_to edges to find the full chain.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: The TS linker already walks the full chain in tracer.ts (DFS through imports). tracePath stores intermediate file paths. The work is to promote those entries from edge properties to first-class module nodes with delegates_to edges between them.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Triple update required — db/types.go, scanner/validate.go, db/schema.go CHECK constraints. Missing one causes silent validation failures.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Schema version auto-migrates via db.InitSchema(). Bump from 3→4. No manual migration script needed.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Scanner options are arbitrary map[string]interface{} passed via ScanInput.options JSON. Config YAML key names must match TypeScript field names exactly (learned from tsconfig/tsConfigPath mismatch bug).

author: mjn
text: FACT: abacus init auto-detects scanners from package.json deps. Will need to generate default moduleClassification when linker-ts is detected.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: TS linker 4-module pipeline: index.ts (IO) → parser.ts (ts-morph) → tracer.ts (DFS) → matcher.ts (Prisma resolution). Module node emission goes in parser.ts where edges are currently built.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Depth-aware cache in tracer.ts is performance-critical. Module classification adds O(tracePath × patterns) per route which is trivial vs AST parsing.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Barrel file noise (repos/index.ts re-exporting 80+ repos) is a known issue. Classification patterns should NOT match barrel/index files. Consider excluding **/index.ts from module classification.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: nodes.go:queryNodesCmd() is a factory. Just call it with db.NodeModule. May need custom column for ROLE (extracted from properties JSON).

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Scanner test fixtures need NO node_modules, NO tsconfig.json, NO installed dependencies. Pure AST analysis. 5 files ~100 lines is sufficient.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Plan review found: (1) GetConnected depth regression — module nodes between routes and entities break depth-2 queries, need edge-kind filtering. (2) Schema migration is destructive — InitSchema drops all tables on version mismatch, destroying manual/agent nodes. (3) Configurable classification is YAGNI — hardcoded heuristics suffice for now. (4) Node ID should use file path, not role, for stability across reclassification.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Applied plan review feedback. 12 recommendations processed across 4 beads. Key changes: (1) Eliminated Bead 2 entirely — no role classification, no config. (2) Keep touches_entity as summary edge alongside delegates_to chain. (3) Added edge-kind filter to GetConnected + composite index + migration warning + bulk upsert to Bead 1. (4) Node ID uses file path, not role. (5) ignorePaths enforced in linker. (6) edge_kinds param exposed in MCP graph_context.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: GetConnected edge-kind filter uses fmt.Sprintf to build the CTE query with optional AND e.kind IN (...) clauses. The kindArgs are duplicated in the args slice because the filter appears in both UNION branches of the recursive CTE.

author: mjn
text: FACT: GetConnected step-2 (edge fetch) intentionally does NOT filter by edge kind — it returns ALL edges between connected nodes. The filter only affects traversal (which nodes are reachable), not the final edge set.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: scan.go BulkUpsertEdges replaces per-edge InsertEdge loop. FK violations are now logged+skipped (built into BulkUpsertEdges) rather than collected as warnings. This is a behavior change but acceptable since FK violations indicate data issues.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Single source of truth for graph kinds — db.AllNodeKinds and db.AllEdgeKinds slices in types.go. validate.go derives its maps from these slices at init time. stats.go and mcp/server.go iterate AllNodeKinds. Adding a new kind now requires updating only (1) types.go constants + All*Kinds slice, (2) schema.go CHECK constraint + version bump. The validate.go sync point is eliminated.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Edge-kind filter on recursive CTE — inject AND e.kind IN (...) into both UNION branches of the bidirectional CTE. kindArgs must be duplicated in the args slice (once per branch). Filter controls traversal reachability only; step-2 edge fetch returns ALL edge types between connected nodes. Args order: [nodeID, maxDepth, ...kindArgs, maxDepth, ...kindArgs].

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: stats.go and mcp/server.go had hardcoded kind lists that silently excluded new kinds. Fixed by using db.AllNodeKinds. When adding graph vocabulary, always grep for hardcoded kind enumerations across the codebase.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Module emission in parser.ts follows a post-processing pattern — after emitting the summary touches_entity edge, iterate tracePath to build module nodes and delegates_to chain. Three dedup sets: seenEdges (shared), seenModules (node dedup). Chain logic: skip tracePath[0] (route file), skip index files (barrel noise), skip ignorePaths matches. Last module→entity edge uses touches_entity (not delegates_to).

author: mjn
text: FACT: processRoutes signature now takes 5 params (added ignorePaths: string[] = []). Return type changed from {edges, warnings, filesScanned} to {nodes, edges, warnings, filesScanned}. ScanOutput.nodes changed from never[] to ScanNode[]. 36 tests passing (32 existing + 4 new).

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: modules.go is a 1-line init() calling queryNodesCmd(db.NodeModule, 'modules', ...) — exact same factory pattern as routes/entities/pages. No extra columns needed for modules (no equivalent to METHOD/FIELDS/PATH).

author: mjn
text: FACT: GraphContextInput now has EdgeKinds []string field. CLI graph command has --edge-kinds flag (StringSlice). Both convert []string → []db.EdgeKind before passing to GetConnected. When empty/nil, all edge kinds are traversed (backward compat).

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Trace-to-graph materialization — convert a flat ordered tracePath array into linked graph nodes and edges using post-processing: (1) filter entries (skip route file at [0], skip barrel/index files, skip ignorePaths), (2) normalize file paths to stable module IDs (relative, forward-slash, ext-stripped, namespaced), (3) dedup nodes via seenModules Set, (4) build delegates_to chain using prev-pointer pattern (let prevId = routeNodeId, advance through chainFiles), (5) terminal edge uses touches_entity kind to cross the module→entity domain boundary. Keep summary edge (route→entity touches_entity) alongside detailed chain for backward compat.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Factory pattern for CLI query commands scales linearly — queryNodesCmd(kind, use, short) now serves 4 node kinds (route, entity, page, module). Adding a new queryable kind requires only a 1-line init() file. MCP query tools follow the same pattern: one-liner handler delegating to queryNodesByKind(). This means adding a 6th node kind in future is a 2-file, 4-line change (modules.go + server.go registration).

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Edge-kind filter (EdgeKinds []string on GraphContextInput, --edge-kinds StringSlice on CLI graph) enables focused traversal without depth regression. When module nodes add intermediate hops, depth-2 queries that previously reached entities now stop at modules. Filter to ['touches_entity'] to get the old behavior, or ['delegates_to','touches_entity'] for the full chain. Nil/empty means all kinds (backward compat). Conversion: []string → []db.EdgeKind at API boundary via direct type cast (zero-cost in Go since EdgeKind is string).

author: mjn
text: FACT: TS linker ScanNode interface (types.ts) is MISSING label and source fields that Go's ScanNode struct requires. ValidateOutput at validate.go:63 checks label != '' — module nodes will fail validation. Also scan.go link-phase loop (lines 214-273) only calls BulkUpsertEdges, never BulkUpsertNodes — module nodes are silently dropped even if validation passes. Both must be fixed before the feature works end-to-end. Filed as follow-up bugs.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Reverse-import resolution (second pass for oRPC contracts) does NOT emit module nodes or delegates_to edges — only summary touches_entity. This is intentional: the tracePath starts from the handler file (not the contract), so the delegation chain wouldn't accurately represent the route→entity path. Routes resolved via reverse-import lack intermediate module visibility. Documented as known limitation.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: TS ScanNode interface must mirror Go ScanNode struct field-for-field. Missing label/source fields caused validation failure at validate.go:63. Fix: add label and source to interface, set label=name and source='scan' on emitted module nodes.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Link-phase scanner loop in scan.go must ingest nodes BEFORE edges — BulkUpsertNodes before DeleteEdgesBySourceScanner/BulkUpsertEdges. FK constraints on edges.src_id/dst_id reference nodes.id, so nodes must exist first. Guard with len(out.Nodes) > 0 to skip when linker emits no nodes.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: runScanPipeline test helper was missing BulkUpsertNodes for link-phase output — module nodes were silently dropped. Fixed by mirroring scan.go lines 256-263: ingest out.Nodes before edges to satisfy FK constraints. Parameterized as runScanPipelineForFixture(t, fixturePath) for multi-fixture support.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Module-test fixture produces exactly 8 nodes (2 routes, 2 entities, 4 modules) and 8 edges (2 route→service delegates_to, 2 service→repo delegates_to, 2 repo→entity touches_entity, 2 route→entity summary touches_entity). Barrel file (repositories/index.ts) correctly excluded — no module node emitted for it.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Abacus is the MAP, not the DRIVER. It answers questions (genesis query) and records facts (action write-back). The coding agent orchestrates — reads the graph, writes code, then tells Abacus what it built. Abacus never orchestrates or generates code.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Three-way step classification: COVERED (step matches existing Action — skip), WIRABLE (no Action but matching routes/entities exist — agent creates Action linking them), NEW (no matching infrastructure — agent queries genesis of similar entity, reads those files as pattern, implements new code, writes back to Abacus).

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Pattern reproduction (D) is emergent, not stored. Graph points to files via genesis query. Agent reads the files and generalizes the pattern itself. No archetype/blueprint abstraction in Abacus. Consistent with graph-as-index philosophy.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Action population (C) is a side effect of the agent workflow, not a separate bootstrapping phase. As the agent wires steps to existing infrastructure (WIRABLE) or implements new features (NEW), it writes Actions back to Abacus. The graph grows organically through use.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Implementation order: B (agent skill) first — easiest to verify, forces building the right queries. A (genesis MCP tool) emerges from B's needs. C (action population) is natural extension of A+B. D (pattern reproduction) is emergent from the agent reading files pointed to by the genesis query.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Genesis query is read-only. Action creation is a write-back from the agent after work is done. The agent tells Abacus: step text, route refs, entity refs, source file. Abacus stores it. Future queries benefit.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Existing plugin commands (abacus-scan.md, abacus-coverage.md) use markdown with YAML frontmatter (description, argument-hint) and numbered steps. Follow same structure. Commands live in .claude-plugin/commands/ and filenames become slash command names.

author: mjn
text: FACT: match_step returns MatchResult with tier (exact/fuzzy/suggest), Action (with resolved Routes/Entities/Pages), and Suggestion (pre-filled CreateActionInput for the suggest tier). The Suggestion already contains related routes/entities/pages from FTS5 search — this IS the WIRABLE detection.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Genesis query composes 3 existing services: MatchService.Match (step resolution), GraphRepository.GetConnected (traversal), GraphRepository.Search (entity lookup). Chain extraction is new logic (~50 lines) that walks delegates_to edges to build ordered paths. Total new Go code estimated at 100-150 lines.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: MCP tool registration follows AddTool pattern in server.go. Input struct with jsonschema tags. Handler gets AbacusServer receiver with repo, actions, matcher fields. CLI command follows cobra pattern — can be standalone file like modules.go. JSON output via PrintJSON helper.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION (SpecFlow): Classification mapping gap — match tiers (exact/fuzzy/suggest) don't map cleanly to COVERED/WIRABLE/NEW. Resolution: exact → COVERED. suggest with non-empty RelatedContext.Routes or Entities → WIRABLE. suggest with empty context → NEW. fuzzy → treat as informational overlay, fall through to suggest-tier logic for classification.

author: mjn
text: DECISION (SpecFlow): Entity extraction is agent-side (LLM reasoning), NOT a new tool. The agent is an LLM — extracting 'notification' from 'the user creates a notification' is trivial for it. No abacus.extract_entities tool needed. Document this as a prompt instruction in the skill.

author: mjn
text: DECISION (SpecFlow): Feature file parsing is agent-side. The agent reads the .feature file and extracts step texts itself. No abacus.parse_feature tool needed — the agent can handle simple Gherkin parsing. Scenario Outlines: match against template step with <placeholder> as {string}. Background steps: classify once globally.

author: mjn
text: FACT (SpecFlow): Exemplar selection for NEW steps — agent should query abacus.stats to see entity count, then abacus.query_entities to list entities, then pick one and call graph_context with edge_kinds=[delegates_to,touches_entity] to check for delegation chain completeness. First entity with delegates_to edges wins. This is O(N) worst case but entities are small (179 in hourly).

author: mjn
text: FACT (SpecFlow): Idempotency — if agent runs /abacus-genesis on same feature file twice, WIRABLE steps will try create_action again and fail. Skill must instruct: check if action exists (via match_step) before creating. If exists, skip or update.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION (SpecFlow): graph_context at depth=5 with all edge kinds may return enormous subgraphs. For pattern discovery, filter to edge_kinds=[delegates_to,touches_entity] only. This traces the delegation chain without noise from uses_route, on_page, etc. The composite tool should default to these edge kinds.

author: mjn
text: FACT (SpecFlow): After code generation, newly created files won't appear in graph until re-scan. Action refs may point to nonexistent nodes temporarily. This is acceptable — agent should create the Action with anticipated node IDs, then scan fills them in. Graph is eventually consistent, not immediately consistent.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Genesis skill uses 3 input modes parsed from argument string — quoted text → single step classification, .feature path → bulk classification with table output, --entity flag → full implementation shape. All modes compose the same MCP tools (match_step, graph_context, query_entities, stats, create_action) in different sequences.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Fuzzy tier (tier=fuzzy) is treated as informational — the agent reports candidates but falls through to suggest-tier logic for actual classification. This avoids a 4th classification bucket and keeps the COVERED/WIRABLE/NEW taxonomy clean.

author: mjn
text: FACT: CLI match command strips Suggestion.Context from JSON output (suggestionJSON struct only has name/label/patterns). MCP match_step returns full MatchResult including RelatedContext with routes/entities/pages. WIRABLE detection only works via MCP tools, which is correct for the skill.

author: mjn
text: FACT: test_repos/hourly has 0 delegates_to edges and 0 module nodes — linker-ts hasnt been run. Pattern discovery shows touches_entity edges (route to entity) but not the full delegation chain. Graph explodes at depth 3 without edge-kind filtering (674 nodes, 61K edges). MCP graph_context supports edge_kinds filter, CLI graph does not yet.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: test_repos/hourly config should use relative paths (../../scanners/...) not hardcoded absolute paths. exec.Command does NOT expand env vars, so ${ABACUS_SCANNERS_PATH} syntax won't work in config.yaml. Relative paths work because CWD is set to the project root during scan.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: When building Claude Code plugin skills that compose MCP tools, keep all intelligence (entity extraction, Gherkin parsing, pattern generalization) in the skill prompt, not in new tools. Decision boundary: if the task requires access to external state (database, filesystem, graph), it needs a tool. If it is pure text reasoning, let the agent do it. This avoids tool proliferation and leverages LLM strengths.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Fuzzy tier from match_step is informational only — it should NOT be treated as a 4th classification bucket. The mental model 'fuzzy = separate category' is the natural wrong assumption. Correct flow: fuzzy candidates shown for context, then fall through to suggest-tier logic (check suggestion.context for routes/entities) to determine WIRABLE vs NEW.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Exemplar-based pattern discovery — when a user needs to create something NEW, find an existing fully-wired example from their own codebase rather than generating boilerplate. Algorithm: (1) extract entity hint from step text (LLM reasoning), (2) search graph for matching entity, (3) if none, iterate entities and pick first with delegates_to edges, (4) traverse graph_context with depth=5 and edge_kinds filter, (5) present delegation chain as ordered file list. The system teaches users their own project conventions.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: CLI/MCP parity gap is a systemic issue, not a one-off bug. Two manifestations: (1) CLI match strips Suggestion.Context making WIRABLE detection impossible, (2) CLI graph lacks --edge-kinds flag causing graph explosion. Root cause: CLI uses reduced projection structs (suggestionJSON) instead of serializing domain types directly. Fix: either serialize full domain types or enforce parity via tests that cross-reference CLI flags against MCP parameters. Same PR should add both CLI flag and MCP parameter.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Three systemic issues underlie most validation problems: (1) CLI/MCP parity not enforced — MCP gets capabilities CLI lacks, causing interface-dependent behavior. (2) Stale artifacts not detected — old binaries and old schema DBs produce confusing downstream symptoms. Fix: embed commit SHA via ldflags, check schema version on DB open. (3) Path resolution has no canonical rule — relative paths resolve to CWD, not config file location. Fix: establish rule that all config paths are relative to config file directory.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used StepMatcher interface in graph package to break import cycle (graph→match→graph). match.MatchService implements the interface via adapter. Wiring happens in MCP server and CLI.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Go import cycle breaking via dependency inversion — graph package defines StepMatcher interface, match package implements it as GenesisAdapter. Wiring layer (MCP server, CLI) bridges them. This is idiomatic Go for circular dependency resolution.

author: mjn
text: FACT: GenesisService composes 3 existing services into a single call. Chain extraction is ~60 lines using DFS with backtracking from route nodes through delegates_to edges, terminating at entities via touches_entity. Cycle-safe via visited set per-DFS.

Key findings: (1) gherkinPatternsFromNode duplicated between graph and match packages — extract to db.GraphNode method, (2) DFS append aliasing is correct but fragile — use explicit copy, (3) GenesisService should be singleton on AbacusServer for consistency. author: mjn
text: DECISION: Sanitize at caller site (genesis.go) not in Search() itself, because FuzzyMatcher intentionally passes FTS5 OR syntax to Search. SanitizeFTS5Query wraps in double quotes to treat input as literal phrase.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Added GherkinPatterns() as a method on db.GraphNode rather than a standalone function, since both graph and match already import db. Eliminates 2 private duplicates with zero new dependencies.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Two FTS5 sanitization strategies for different use cases. (1) Tokenize+OR for broad fuzzy search: strip non-alphanumeric, remove stop words, join with OR — used by FuzzyMatcher for BM25 ranked results. (2) Double-quote wrapping for exact phrase lookup: escape internal quotes (""), wrap in double quotes — used by genesis entity search where you want the literal name. Strategy (1) is destructive (loses special chars, splits words); strategy (2) preserves the input as-is. Both prevent FTS5 injection but serve different query intents. Key: the Search() function itself stays generic (accepts raw FTS5 syntax); callers choose the sanitization strategy.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: When two Go packages (A and B) have identical private functions operating on a shared type from package C, add a method to the type in C. Both A and B already import C, so zero new dependencies. Example: graph.gherkinPatternsFromNode(node) and match.extractGherkinPatterns(node) both operated on db.GraphNode — replaced with db.GraphNode.GherkinPatterns() method. This eliminates duplication AND improves discoverability (method appears in type's doc). Prefer methods over package-level functions when the logic is intrinsic to the type's data.

author: mjn

author: mjn

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Go append aliasing: when append(slice, elem) has spare capacity, it returns a slice backed by the SAME array. Sibling iterations of a for loop can see mutations from earlier iterations' recursive calls. Explicit copy-then-set eliminates this class of bug entirely.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: ~/.abacus/scanners/ as the standard install location for scanner dist files. Probe order: (1) ABACUS_SCANNERS_PATH env var, (2) ~/.abacus/scanners/, (3) binary-relative (dev mode). make install builds scanners via build-all.sh then copies dist/ dirs to ~/.abacus/scanners/. This follows the XDG-ish convention of user-local tool data in ~/.<toolname>/.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: FTS5 BM25 ranking across multiple indexed columns (name, label, properties) causes entity name searches to return wrong results. Properties JSON contains field names like userId that outrank the actual entity named User. Fix: use column-scoped FTS5 syntax (name:"User") to restrict matching to the name column only. This is critical for any FTS5 index that includes a JSON properties column.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Applied plan review feedback. 9 recommendations processed. Key changes: (1) Dropped TraversalDirection type entirely — YAGNI, no repository changes needed. (2) Merged 2 beads into 1: fix is ~15 lines in genesis.go only, using GetEdgesTo + edgeKinds=[delegates_to]. (3) Added fanout cap (50) and SrcID dedup for DoS prevention. (4) Deferred multi-seed CTE, composite indexes, GetNodesByIDs as potential follow-ups if simple fix isn't fast enough.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Plan review with 4 agents (architecture, simplicity, security, performance) reduced a 2-bead plan to 1 bead with ~15 lines changed instead of ~80. Key insight from simplicity reviewer: GetConnected is not broken — genesis was passing the wrong edge kinds. Don't build generic abstractions when the specific problem has a targeted fix.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used edgeKinds override approach instead of TraversalDirection. Entity case sets edgeKinds=[delegates_to] only, preventing touches_entity from entering the recursive CTE. entityTouchEdges are injected after traversal so ExtractDelegationChains can still terminate chains at the entity.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Hub-node explosion has TWO layers: (1) modules with touches_entity to many entities — fixed by not passing touches_entity to CTE. (2) Hub modules as traversal seeds — bidirectional delegates_to traversal goes BACKWARD and finds every route that delegates to the hub. Fix: only use route nodes (prefix 'route:') as traversal seeds. Modules are discovered through forward delegates_to from routes.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Genesis entity queries (abacus genesis --entity User) returned 570 routes instead of ~20. Two-layer hub-node explosion: (1) touches_entity edges in the recursive CTE caused bidirectional traversal to fan out through hub modules (authz.middleware) to every entity, pulling in the entire graph. (2) Even after removing touches_entity from the CTE, hub modules used as traversal seeds caused backward delegates_to traversal to pull in every route that delegates to them. Both layers compound: hub module connects to all entities AND all routes delegate to it.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Two-step directed entity lookup in genesis — (1) GetEdgesTo(entityID, touches_entity) for single-hop reverse lookup of who touches the entity, (2) filter to route-only seeds (strings.HasPrefix 'route:'), (3) GetConnected(routeID, depth, [delegates_to]) for delegation chain traversal. Never pass touches_entity to the recursive CTE. Inject the touching edges post-traversal so ExtractDelegationChains can still terminate chains at entities. This pattern applies whenever a graph has hub nodes with high fan-out on one edge kind.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Plan review (4 agents: architecture, simplicity, security, performance) reduced a 2-bead/80-line plan to a 1-bead/15-line fix. Key insight from simplicity reviewer: 'GetConnected is not broken — genesis was giving it the wrong problem.' Don't build generic abstractions (TraversalDirection type) when the specific problem has a targeted fix (change which edge kinds you pass). YAGNI saved ~65 lines of unnecessary code.

author: mjn
text: FACT: In Abacus graphs, hub nodes exist at two levels: (1) middleware modules like authz.middleware that have touches_entity edges to nearly every entity (they import PrismaClient and check permissions across all models), (2) the same modules receive delegates_to edges from nearly every route (all routes use auth middleware). This dual-hub pattern means ANY traversal passing through them — forward or backward, via any edge kind — risks pulling in the entire graph. The only safe approach is to avoid using them as traversal seeds entirely.

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used ID prefix filtering (strings.HasPrefix 'route:') instead of GetNode+kind check to identify route nodes from GetEdgesTo results. Rationale: (1) avoids N GetNode calls, (2) Abacus node IDs are namespaced by convention (route:, entity:, module:, page:), (3) this convention is enforced by all scanners. Tradeoff: couples genesis to the ID naming convention, but this convention is already load-bearing across the codebase (scanner IDs, CLI output, test fixtures).

author: mjn

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Key ts-morph APIs for binding resolution: importDecl.getNamedImports() returns ImportSpecifier[] with .getName(). For barrel re-exports: sourceFile.getExportDeclarations() + exportDecl.getNamedExports() + exportDecl.getModuleSpecifierSourceFile(). These are stable, well-documented APIs.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Current tracer DFS entry point is traceImports(sourceFile, entityByName, options, cache). The binding-aware change adds a 'bindings: string[] | null' parameter. null = follow all (current behavior / fallback). string[] = only follow these named bindings through barrel files.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: matcher.ts findPrismaAccesses() currently scans entire SourceFile. Adding scopeToFunctions param: when provided, use sourceFile.getFunction(name) or sourceFile.getVariableDeclaration(name) to find the body, then walk only that subtree for CallExpressions. Fall back to full-file scan when function not found.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Cache key change from filePath to (filePath, bindings) means the cache Map type changes. Consider Map<string, Map<string, {entities, remainingDepth}>> where outer key is filePath and inner key is sorted binding names joined by comma. Empty string inner key = full-file scan (fallback/legacy).

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Hourly barrel is 835 lines. Factory pattern: buildPrismaRepositories() returns object with 94 repos. Destructured: export const { userRepository, ... } = _repos. Services import specific bindings: import { permissionGrantRepository } from '../repositories/index.js'. Routes mostly import types only. getExportedDeclarations() resolves factory bindings to VariableDeclaration in same file (not different file like re-exports).

author: mjn
text: FACT: Cache safety for binding-filtered traces: DO NOT write to cache when tracing with bindings (the result is a subset, would poison other callers wanting different bindings). Only cache full traces (null bindings). Children of filtered files ARE cached normally since they're traced fully. Barrel file itself is never cached — it's just indirection.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Key ts-morph APIs: importDecl.getNamedImports() → ImportSpecifier[] with .getName(). sourceFile.getExportedDeclarations() → Map<string, Declaration[]> resolves through re-exports. ExportSpecifier.getLocalTargetDeclarations() → Node[]. For factory: VariableDeclaration.getNameNode() checks ObjectBindingPattern, then trace to factory function's return object properties.

author: mjn
text: INVESTIGATION: Plan deepened with research from 4 agents. Key improvements: (1) Discovered hourly barrel is factory pattern (835 lines, destructured exports) — plan now handles both re-export AND factory barrels with two strategies. (2) Tests must use in-memory ts-morph (no fixture dirs) — bead updated with exact test patterns. (3) Cache safety: binding-filtered traces must skip cache write to avoid poisoning other callers. (4) Concrete insertion points identified: tracer.ts lines 103-120 (import loop), parser.ts line 178 (trace call).

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: ts-morph in-memory filesystem does NOT support directory-to-index.ts resolution. Imports must use './services/index' explicitly, not './services'. Also, barrel files need import+re-export pattern (import then export) rather than 'export { X } from' syntax for the tracer to follow them, because tracer uses getImportDeclarations() not getExportDeclarations().

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Used it.fails() for RED tests (1, 2, 5) so vitest CI stays green. These tests assert the DESIRED behavior (filtered entities) and currently fail because the tracer returns the unfiltered set. When aba-cl6.2 implements binding-aware filtering, these tests will start passing and it.fails() should be changed to it().

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Binding-filtered traces skip BOTH cache read and cache write for the filtered file. Children (e.g., user.service.ts) are still cached normally since they're traced with full depth. This prevents cache poisoning where Route A traces barrel with ['UserService'] → caches {User}, then Route B asks for ['PostService'] and gets wrong cache hit.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: ts-morph getExportedDeclarations() correctly resolves through import-then-re-export chains. For 'import { X } from ./y; export { X };' barrels, getExportedDeclarations().get('X') returns the original declaration in ./y, not a local binding. This is the key API that enables re-export barrel resolution without heuristics.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Factory barrel resolution uses 6-step AST traversal: (1) find ObjectBindingPattern with target binding, (2) resolve initializer identifier to its definition, (3) get the CallExpression, (4) resolve callee to FunctionDeclaration, (5) find ReturnStatement with ObjectLiteral → property matching binding name, (6) trace the property's CallExpression callee back to its ImportSpecifier source file. Each step has a try/catch fallback to null → full trace.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: For import aliases (import { Foo as Bar }), the TypeScript compiler node has propertyName.text='Foo' (export name) and name.text='Bar' (local name). To get the correct export name for getExportedDeclarations() lookup, use: compilerNode.propertyName?.text ?? getName(). This is critical for binding-aware resolution correctness.

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Real-world factory barrels use ternary (ConditionalExpression) initializers — must extract CallExpression from both whenTrue/whenFalse branches

author: mjn
text: LEARNED: Hourly repo uses default imports (import createFoo from './foo.js') alongside named imports — must handle Node.isImportClause() in addition to Node.isImportSpecifier() for factory binding resolution

author: mjn
text: DECISION: Binding-filtered traces skip both cache read AND write to prevent partial results poisoning the cache. Child files traced from resolved bindings ARE cached normally since they represent full traces.

author: mjn
text: FACT: Integration results — touches_entity edges reduced from ~19K to 10,049 (84% reduction in linker edges). GET /health at 91 edges is structural (app.ts imports everything), not a barrel issue.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Forward-only BFS using GetEdgesFrom replaces GetConnected for entity mode. GetConnected remains for step/node modes where bidirectional traversal is correct (you want to discover which routes connect to a given entity through any path).

author: mjn
text: FACT: GetEdgesFrom hits the edges.src_id index — individual lookups are fast. With fanout cap of 50 seeds and depth 10, worst case is ~500 queries, each O(log n). The CTE approach was 1 query but returned wrong results.

author: mjn
text: PATTERN: Factory barrel resolution requires handling ternary ConditionalExpression (extract CallExpression from both branches) and default imports (ImportClause, not just ImportSpecifier). Both missed by unit tests, caught by integration testing against hourly.
